recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed unless the external Patient/$merge link or high-level Patient-page pointer becomes stale; future substantive Patient/$merge behavior changes should be made in HL7/admin-incubator.
issue_request: FHIR-19687 was a Published PA change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking how searches and patient compartments should behave when a Patient has been linked, merged, or unlinked. The resolution distinguished cross-system linking from intra-system merge handling and expected merge behavior to move data/references to the new Patient, mark the old Patient inactive with a link, and use OperationOutcome guidance for in-progress or redirected search cases.
initial_application: The detailed PA Merge Operation work and PA minutes supplied the intended behavior. Core source was explicitly changed by 96213161a5, which added the Patient/$merge OperationDefinition, examples, and Patient operations list entry, and by 389af0dfa6, which added extended merge usage notes; b494aee51b merged those FHIR-19687 changes.
additional_context: Patient remains active in core, but b487fdda4b later removed Patient-merge from the core Patient operations list and changed Patient and Parameters links to the Administrative Incubator Patient/$merge page. The legacy operation-Patient-merge-notes.xml file is still present but no longer referenced by the active core Patient page or Patient operations list. Later same-family Patient merge audits for FHIR-38183, FHIR-38877, and FHIR-38888 are already on the combined branch and support the same build-scope conclusion.
reconciliation: No core source change was made. The active Patient narrative points to the external Patient/$merge page, and the current linked external page contains the source/target merge semantics, source inactive/replaced-by handling, reference rewiring, OperationOutcome guidance, and post-merge search expectations needed for FHIR-19687.
